A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Intention-Conditioned Flow Occupancy Models by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original ExORL and OGBench experiments, RT-1/SimplerEnv evaluation, latent visualizations, and multiple ablations in Sections 5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds prediction-error measurements, latent-variable ablations, dataset-diversity analysis, and suboptimal-data experiments.

M1.justification: The main InFOM algorithm remains unchanged. Appendix F.4 adds a tested discrete-intention variant with a deterministic encoder, nearest-neighbor quantization, and VQ loss; F.5 adds a posterior-sampling variant of critic distillation. These are auxiliary procedural adaptations.

E1.justification: All benchmark tasks and environments are retained, including the robotics evaluation already present in v2. Appendix F.10 adds a low-quality fine-tuning scenario using reward-filtered ExORL transitions on cheetah run and quadruped jump; the other additions reuse existing coverage.

E2.justification: Figures 11–12 add discrete-intention and posterior-sampling InFOM variants as evaluated comparators. The eight main baselines and existing HILP + FOM/FB + FOM comparisons remain. The added diffusion, VAE, and GAN discussion cites prior results rather than reporting new evaluations of those methods.

E3.justification: The appendix substantially expands evaluation procedures: prediction MSE over 100 trajectories with 400 generated states per trajectory, diversity measured using state-space discretization at 10^-2 resolution, and reward-quantile filtering followed by sampling 500K fine-tuning transitions. The existing benchmark budgets, metrics, and aggregation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct prediction-error comparisons, discrete-versus-continuous intentions, prior-versus-posterior sampling, dataset-diversity analysis, and sensitivity to fine-tuning data quality. These investigate several previously untested questions. Existing policy-extraction, dataset-size, sample-count, and hyperparameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix F.8 introduces Pearson correlation estimation for dataset size versus state coverage. The existing eight-seed state-based and four-seed image-based mean-and-standard-deviation reporting remains unchanged; no new confidence-interval or formal significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Table 4 and retained plots preserve their results. New experiments report lower prediction MSE than both FOM comparators, discrete-intention declines of 11% on ExORL and 78% on OGBench, a 7% posterior-sampling difference, diversity correlations of 0.67 and 0.86, and retention of 9%/85% of original performance at reward quantiles 0.2/0.8. These are added results, not improved scores for the unchanged main evaluation.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix C.1 explicitly introduce λ≥1 for the KL-weighted likelihood-bound inequality, add a constrained-optimization/Lagrangian formulation for λ≥0, and assert an input-rescaling justification. The existing consistency assumption, information-bottleneck derivation, and GPI analysis are largely retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: intention-conditioned flow occupancy modeling and implicit GPI for effective pre-training and fine-tuning. The headline 1.8× median return improvement and 36% success-rate improvement claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations favoring continuous intentions, treating prior/posterior similarity as robustness to unseen latents, and identifying poor-reward fine-tuning data as a failure condition. F.8–F.9 justify dataset size as a diversity proxy and revise the size-effect explanation from avoiding unseen future states to avoiding unseen intentions.

D1.justification: New experimental details include a 256-entry codebook, straight-through gradients, distillation using all discrete latents, prediction-error sampling counts, grid resolution, and reward-filtering instructions. Algorithm 2 clarifies policy initialization. Tables 1–3, hardware and training-time disclosures, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Value Flows, floq, VQ-VAE, and straight-through gradient estimation, and discusses alternative latent priors. It also explains the decision to rely on Farebrother et al.'s generative-model comparisons. The central positioning relative to prior occupancy and intention-learning methods remains stable.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and most existing prose are retained. Changes comprise localized explanations, additional appendix subsections and cross-references, pseudocode annotations, wording corrections, removal of duplicated response-oriented text in old F.7, and the ICLR 2026 publication header.

P2.justification: Five new figures—v3 Figures 8, 11, 12, 15, and 18—substantially expand the visual analyses. Existing appendix figures and tables are redistributed, with some plots resized. Old Figure 13 becomes Figure 17 with its vertical-axis label corrected from return to success rate; its plotted values are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added prediction checks and latent-choice ablations strengthen support for existing design decisions, while the suboptimal-data experiment makes an important failure condition explicit. These improve an already extensively evaluated paper without changing its main results. The theoretical clarification is incomplete: the assertion that input rescaling permits λ<1 while preserving an ELBO remains unsupported by a derivation.
